> Author: researcher (vfx-deep-research workflow) · claude-sonnet-5-5 · low · 2026-10-12

# P1 Elements: COMPOSITION + CAMERA/SCREEN effects + perception science

Scope: composition (layers, density), camera/screen effects (shake, hit-stop, kick/zoom, slow motion, flash, vignette, aberration, radial blur), perception science (attention, clutter, crowding).
Framework words used: gameplay, shape, value, colour, timing, composition. Timing words: windup, punch, crescendo, follow-through, dissipation.

**Run limits (read this first)**
- The shared WebSearch budget (200 per turn) ran out mid-run. Planned searches not run: 2020+ hit-stop talks, tier-A VFX layering talks, vignette/aberration/radial-blur studies. All later pages were fetched from known URLs or links found on pages already read. No archive or proxy service was used.
- Publisher full texts (Springer, Nature, JoV, ScienceDirect) were blocked. For 5 perception papers only the abstract record (Europe PMC) was read. Marked "abstract" below.
- No talk video was watched or transcribed. For Eiserloh the official slide deck text was read. For Nijman and Jonasson/Purho no primary text was reachable.
- Numbers marked "computed" are my arithmetic on a cited formula. Frame-to-ms conversions assume 60 fps and are inference.

### 2.1 Element table (required format)

Evidence key: study | preprint | industry practice | spec | inference.
"Source, tier and year" lists the source id first.

#### A. Camera and screen effects

| timing | Hit-stop (freeze animation at contact) present vs absent | Hits feel solid and weighty. Without it, attacks feel soft and powerless; miss vs hit and light vs heavy blur together. | Raises punch energy sharply for a tiny time cost. | Games with no hit-stop (2 of 16, ranks 39 and 40) had under 70% "IF attitude" (share of positive impact-feel comments). Almost all other games used it. No coefficient or effect size given. | Freeze marks the contact moment, tells severity, and creates rhythm. Presence was compared between top 8 and bottom 8 games; correlational, n=16, Chinese-language Steam comments, Naive Bayes classifier. | preprint (feature-presence comparison, not an experiment) | S01, A preprint, 2022 [V: confirmed - arXiv text: Sacred Citadel and Draw Slasher (ranks 39, 40) lack hit stop, "less than 70 %" IF attitude; 16 games; Naive Bayes; arXiv comments say accepted at IEEE CTSoc GEM 2022] |
| timing | Hit-stop length scaled to hit strength | Light hits feel quick and rhythmic; heavy hits feel heavy. | timing | Camera shake (screen shake) as trauma that decays | Short, readable "something big happened". Escalation is perceptible, so small, medium and large events feel different. | Main energy dial for explosions and heavy hits. | Trauma level in [0,1]. Damage or stress adds trauma: += 0.2 or 0.5. Trauma decreases linearly over time. Shake = trauma^2 or trauma^3. Slide example: trauma .30 / .60 / .90 = 3% / 22% / 73% shake (these percentages equal trauma^3; computed check: .027 / .216 / .729; squared would give 9% / 36% / 81%). Working code (Bevy): decay 0.5 per second, exponent 2.0, max roll 10 deg, max translation 20 px, noise speed 20, +0.4 per event. Computed from those constants: one +0.4 event at t=0 shows 0.16 of max (1.6 deg, 3.2 px) and ends after 0.8 s. | Spring-and-damper feel (Eiserloh's words on the slide); exponent makes small events subtle and big ones violent while escalations stay perceptible. | industry practice (maker talk 2016, pre-2020); Bevy constants are a third-party implementation | S02 A 2016 (pre-2020); S23 C [V: confirmed - slides: trauma in [0,1], += 0.2 or 0.5, linear decrease, trauma2 or t3, ".30, .60, .90 means 3%, 22%, 73%" (matches cubic), "spring and damper"; Bevy page: decay 0.5/s, exponent 2.0, 10 deg, 20 px, noise speed 20, +0.4 per hit] |
| timing | Shake signal: smoothed noise vs random per frame | Smoothed noise feels better; random is jittery. | Smoothed noise gives tunable roughness without raising amplitude. | Perlin noise, one seed per axis (seed, seed+1 ...). Slide reasons: feels better, works with pause and slow motion, adjustable frequency, reproducible on replay. Newer confirmation: UE5 docs list Perlin pattern for high-intensity shakes and wave pattern for gentle ones (no values). Roblox: RbxCameraShaker samples math.noise per axis; tick advances by dt*roughness; output = noise * magnitude * fade. | Continuous noise has no discontinuities; frequency is a separate knob from amplitude. | industry practice (2016) + spec (UE5) + C implementation | S02 A 2016 (pre-2020); S22 spec; S24 C |

| gameplay | Multimodal stacking (shake + particles + sound together) | A hit felt on several channels feels real; a single channel feels thin. | Stacking raises energy but also the risk of noise. | One-shot particles are "often layered with screen shake and sound" (S03). Song's list of hit-effect channels in the genre: white flash, particles (blood, firework, directional), trails (colour, particle, distortion), impact light, shake, slow motion, sound by weapon and surface. No ideal channel count found. | Redundant cues across senses. | industry practice | S03 A 2021; S07 A maker 2005 |
| gameplay | Amount of juice (feedback amplification) | More is not always better. Extreme juice and zero juice both lowered experience; medium and high were best. In a 2024 experiment, amplifying feedback unexpectedly LOWERED effectance, competence and curiosity motives. | Peak energy must be earned by outcome. | Kao 2020: four versions of one action RPG (none / medium / high / extreme). Kao 2024: N=1,699, pre-registered; feedback that depended on success raised all three motives; amplification lowered them, possibly by undermining agency. Johansen 2021 (N=113): hand-tuned effect set beat baseline (p<0.001); generated sets were preferred in 2 of 6 comparisons; in the adversarial game no generated set was preferred, authors suggest fewer effects suit tension. | Clear action-outcome link and graded success matter more than raw intensity. | study | S05 A 2024; S03 A 2021 (reporting Kao 2020); S04 A 2021 [V: confirmed - Kao 2024: N=1,699, pre-registered, amplification lowered effectance/competence/curiosity, success-dependence raised them, CHI 2024. Johansen and Cook: 113 participants (106 and 112 analysed), expert vs baseline p<0.001, one-third of generated sets beat baseline = 2 of 6, adversarial game "players prefer fewer effects" is the authors' hedged guess ("possible"), not a finding. Kao 2020 still unread] |
| gameplay | Light vs heavy hit feedback | Light: direct, informative cue. Heavy: add decorative layers and reward. | Escalation ladder. | Not numeric. On-hit pattern differs per weapon: spot pattern for fist and blunt, extra directional effect for sharp weapons (BlazBlue Centralfiction). | Feedback proportional to event importance. | industry practice | S01 A preprint 2022 |

#### B. Composition (layers, density)

| heading | element | effect on feeling | effect on energy | numbers or ranges | mechanism | evidence level | source, tier and year |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| composition | Layer count that is rich vs mud | no number found | no number found | **No named source gives a layer count or particle count for "rich vs mud".** Only qualitative: excess makes it hard to learn which elements matter, e.g. a screen full of wobbling particles (S03). Players preferred fewer effects in a tense adversarial game (S04). | Clutter hides the key event (see 2.3 Rosenholtz). | industry practice (qualitative) + inference | S03 A 2021; S04 A 2021 |
| composition | One effect = several channels, each with one job | Reads as one event if shape/flash lead and the rest support. | Core gives punch; secondary gives spread; tertiary gives follow-through. | Concrete channel lists exist (Song: flash, particles, trails, impact light, shake, sound) but no hierarchy or proportion. My mapping to the project layers (primary shape, sparks, smoke, distortion, light, ground mark) is inference. | Redundant channels at different times and sizes. | inference | S07 A maker 2005 (channels); inference |
| composition | Separate flash per impact so rapid hits read as separate | Keeps each hit countable. | Preserves combo rhythm. | Under 5 frames apart (30 fps) hits merge; per-impact flashing particle effect in KUF:TC keeps 2-4 frame spacing readable (S07). | Per-event onset marker. | industry practice | S07 A maker 2005 |
| composition | After-hit persistence | Lingering result prolongs satisfaction after the peak. | Follow-through and dissipation. | "Several seconds" for some after-hit effects (blood, destruction). No exact value. | Persistent evidence of the event. | industry practice | S01 A preprint 2022 |
| composition | Impact light | Lighting the contact point lights both fighters and makes the hit feel physical. | Cheap value punch. | One light source at the impact point (Soul Calibur 2); KUF:TC used a fixed number of directional hit lights for low cost. No intensity number. | Local luminance burst. | industry practice (pre-2020) | S07 A maker 2005 |
| composition | Clear shape beats diffuse shape | Clear, well-defined shape reads as more striking than a diffuse blur. | n/a | No number. Tier C weak, uncredited. Consistent with the pre-attentive shape and size guidance in S15 but needs a tier A VFX source. | Readability. | industry practice (weak) | S26 C weak 2026 |
| composition | Modular components, data-driven assembly (agent-relevant) | n/a | Lets non-artists assemble effects from parts. | Poster describes a few Niagara variants per component type (initiation flash/burst, ground eruption...), assembled from data tables; hundreds of combinations; timing-critical motion locked in curves, only safe parameters (e.g. a Scale float) exposed. No counts given. | Guard-railed parameters keep timing intact. | industry practice (single named poster; needs second source) | S27 C 2026 |
| composition | Density: clumped vs even spacing | Clumped, similar-looking elements around a key element make it hard to read; distinct or separated elements stay readable. | Even distribution reads as ambience; clumps read as intent (inference). | Crowding: critical spacing is about 0.4-0.5 of eccentricity (Bouma, "widely reported"); not a hard law; a target at 10 deg eccentricity can be crowded by items up to 5 deg away. Crowding falls when target and neighbours differ in shape, size, orientation, colour, motion, or when the target is shown about 150 ms before or after the flankers. Crowding rises with similar neighbours and simultaneous presentation. | Peripheral vision pools features; similar neighbours blend. | study (human vision) + inference for effects | S13 A 2011 (pre-2020) [V: confirmed - Whitney and Levi: Bouma "widely reported to be ≈ 0.4-0.5", "varies across studies"; ~150 ms before/after flankers breaks crowding] |

### 2.2 Ranges the sources support (for the agent's first guess; each is inference from the rows above)

| quantity | supported range | basis | caution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hit-stop, light | 7 frames (about 117 ms at 60 fps) as a fighting-game reference; Smash at low damage about 9 f (150 ms) | S01, S29 | Fighting games with fixed 60 fps. Roblox frame rate varies; use time (seconds), not frames. |
| Hit-stop, heavy | about 10 f (167 ms) fighting; up to 30 f (500 ms) cap in Smash Ultimate | S01, S29 | Smash is a fan-wiki formula. Long stops on repeated hits feel like lag. |
| Global freeze for a finisher | about 1 s once (DBFZ ultimate charge, opponent only) | S01 | One example. |
| Gap between countable hits | at least about 5 frames (167 ms at 30 fps), clearly separate at about 8+ (267 ms) | S07 | Measured on a 30 fps clip of one game. |
| Shake shaping | amplitude = trauma^2 or ^3; trauma += 0.2 to 0.5 per event; linear decay | S02 | Decay rate in seconds not on the slides; Bevy uses 0.5 per second. |
| Shake, 2D | translate + rotate | S02 | |
| Shake, 3D | rotate only | S02 | Roblox shaker defaults include position influence 0.15-0.25 (S24); check clipping in third person. |
| Flash | 1-2 frames (weak source); repeated rate at most 3 per second | S26 (weak), S19 | Flash length claim needs a second source. |
| Juice level | aim for the "medium to high" middle and graded by success; avoid extreme | S05, S03 (Kao 2020) | Studies used one action RPG; our game is a different genre. |

### 2.3 Perception science (rated)

Ratings: strong = replicated finding stated in a review or consensus paper; moderate = single well-known experiment, abstract read; weak = indirect for our use.

| claim | what the source says | rating | evidence level | game-VFX use (inference) | source, tier and year |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Abrupt onsets capture attention | Abrupt onsets were the first stimuli shown to capture attention strongly, and consensus statement: certain stimuli (abrupt onsets, colour singletons) automatically generate a priority signal when no specific control settings are in place. | strong | study (consensus review) | A VFX must start with an onset (flash, burst), not fade in, if it must be noticed. | S14 A 2021 [V: confirmed for the consensus sentence (Luck et al.: abrupt onsets and colour singletons "automatically generate a priority signal" absent control settings; paper also says it is unresolved whether onsets can be suppressed). V: unverified for "first stimuli shown to capture attention" (not found in the part read)] |
| Onset of motion captures; ongoing motion does not | Objects that had just started moving were found faster than static ones even though motion was uninformative; sensitivity to onsets alongside relative insensitivity to ongoing motion. | moderate (3 experiments, abstract only) | study | Constant swirling does not attract; the first frame of motion does. Debris that starts moving at the blast is noticed; ambient drift is not. | S12 A 2003 (pre-2020) [V: unverified - Abrams and Christ 2003 abstract not re-opened] |
| Moving and looming stimuli capture; receding does not | Translating and looming (approaching) stimuli capture; receding do not. | moderate (abstract only) | study | Shockwaves and debris coming toward the camera pull attention; shrinking effects do not. | S11 A 2003 (pre-2020) [V: unverified - Franconeri and Simons 2003 abstract not re-opened] |
| Looming is only "possible" in the newer guidance table | Wolfe and Horowitz put expansion/looming under "possible" guiding attribute, colour, motion, orientation and size under "undoubted", luminance onset under "probable". Probably not guiding: luminosity, colour change, optic flow, blur, biological motion. | moderate | study (review) | Rank cues: size and motion first, luminance onset next, looming uncertain, hue change alone weak. | S15 A 2017 [V: confirmed - Table 1 of Wolfe and Horowitz: color, motion, orientation, size undoubted; luminance onset probable; expansion/looming possible; color change, optic flow, luminosity, blur, biological motion probably not guiding. Table says "color change", not "hue change"] |
| Salience depends on context | Perceptual saliency of a stimulus depends on its surrounding context; a saliency map is an effective bottom-up control strategy; inhibition of return stops re-attending the same spot. | strong (classic; abstract only) | study | A spark among many similar sparks is not salient; a distinct one is. | S09 A 2001 (pre-2020) |
| Salience rises with target-distractor difference and distractor-distractor homogeneity, for basic features only | Core rule. Bottom-up salience predicts search only modestly, and poorly when the observer has a goal. | strong | study (review) | Make the key shape differ from the debris in size or brightness; uniform debris makes the hero read stand out. Players with a goal (find the next target) will partly ignore flashy cues. | S15 A 2017 |
| Pop-out has about zero search slope; serial search about 20-50 ms per item | Numbers from the review. | strong | study | Each extra similar-looking item that must be scanned adds roughly 20-50 ms; effects that need scanning are slow to read. | S15 A 2017 [V: corrected - the 20-50 ms/item slope in the paper is for one task (T among Ls), not a general cost for any "similar-looking item"; treat as a rough order of magnitude, not a VFX rule] |
| Salient cues can be suppressed | Evidence that salient colour singletons are proactively suppressed under some conditions; suppression builds over several trials with the same singleton colour; PD marker begins within about 150 ms; suppression found at set size 4 but not 6 or 10 in one study where the singleton then captured attention. | moderate (live debate) | study | A repeated identical flash in the same colour may stop working; vary the cue. With many items on screen the suppression failed in one study. | S14 A 2021 [V: confirmed - PD begins within 150 ms; Wang and Theeuwes 2020: suppression at set size 4, none at 6 and 10, capture at 10; Gaspelin and Luck found suppression at 6, so this is contested] |
| Visual clutter is measurable | Feature Congestion, Subband Entropy, Edge Density correlate with search performance in complex images. | moderate (abstract only) | study | We can compute a clutter score on Studio screenshots as an automated review check (inference; tool not built). | S10 A 2007 (pre-2020) |
| Crowding limits recognition | Spacing about 0.4-0.5 eccentricity; release by dissimilarity; temporal separation about 150 ms; similar neighbours and simultaneous presentation worsen it. | strong | study (review) | Stagger layers by 150 ms or more when the first layer must be read; separate the key hit spark from similar particles by shape, size or colour. | S13 A 2011 (pre-2020) [V: confirmed - same passages as the crowding row above] |
| Contact-then-motion is seen as causation ("launching") | Launching and triggering are distinct perceptual categories with location-specific adaptation. | moderate (abstract only) | study | Supports a short pause at contact then a clear reaction (hit-stop then debris); the mechanism for hit-stop itself is my inference, not tested here. | S16 A 2020 |
| Flash safety | Three flashes per second limit; 10% relative luminance; area 0.006 sr in a 10-degree field. | strong (standard) | spec | Chained explosion flashes must be rate-limited. | S19 spec [V: confirmed - WCAG numbers as above] |
| Players get attention directed by camera control | Dedicated camera control is a top-3 feature in impact feel. | weak (tiny n, correlational) | preprint | Frame the key event; do not follow blindly. | S01 A preprint 2022 |

## 4. Conflicts between sources (newer first)

| topic | newer source says | older source says | what changed / our reading |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Is more juice better? | Kao et al. 2024 (S05, N=1,699): amplification lowered effectance, competence, curiosity; success-dependence raised them. Johansen and Cook 2021 (S04): fewer effects suit a tense adversarial game. | Juice philosophy 2012 (Jonasson and Purho, known only via S04/S03): "constant and bountiful" feedback. Kao 2020 (via S03): medium and high best. | Newer work adds that the amount matters less than being tied to outcome. Treat intensity as scaled by outcome, not maximal by default. |
| Looming and attention | Wolfe and Horowitz 2017 (S15): expansion/looming only "possible"; Luck et al. 2021 (S14): abrupt onsets capture, but capture can be suppressed. | Franconeri and Simons 2003 (S11): looming captures. | Looming is likely real but not rated "undoubted" in the newer table. Do not rely on looming alone; pair it with a luminance onset. |
| Trauma exponent | Bevy example (S23): exponent 2.0. | Eiserloh 2016 (S02): "trauma^2 (or t^3)" while the slide's example percentages match the cubic. | Either is acceptable; cubic is subtler at low trauma. Pick by feel; make it a parameter. |
| Translation shake in 3D | Roblox RbxCameraShaker presets include position influence 0.15-0.25 (S24, tier C). | Eiserloh 2016: 3D translation is "VERY BAD", rotate only. | Not a true conflict: small position influence with large rotation. Test for third-person clipping in Studio. |
| Hit-stop size | Smash Ultimate (S29, tier D): up to 30 frames (500 ms). | GG Xrd (S01): 7-10 frames; Nuclear Throne (S28): 10-20 ms. | Different genres, frame rates and units. No single standard. Scale by damage and by genre; measure feel in our game. |
| Hit-stop as top factor | S01 (2022) ranks hit stop, sound coherence, camera control highest. | S03 (2021) calls hit stop perhaps the best-researched impact feedback but gives only "a few frames". | They agree on importance; neither gives an effect size. S01 is correlational with 16 games. |
| Trauma/hit-stop update after 2016/2013 | Searched for a newer numeric update; none found for Nijman 2013 or Eiserloh 2016. UE5 docs (S22) still teach Perlin patterns; Pichlmair 2021 (S03) still cites Nijman and Jonasson and Purho. | n/a | Classics remain current. No source says they are outdated. |

| Hit-stop frames/ms for Street Fighter 6, other Capcom, and action games | SF6 wikis blocked (Anubis), Dustloop 404, no tier A numbers found; search budget ran out | Record gameplay at 60 fps and count freeze frames; or build a Studio A/B with hit-stop 0, 60, 100, 160, 250 ms on the same blast and have 5-10 people rate weight on phone. |
| Coefficients behind S01 | Paper has no regression; only presence tables and a "<70% IF attitude" figure | Cannot be recovered. Run our own rating study. |
| Layer count and particle count for "rich vs mud" | No named source gives one | Build the same blast with 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 channels; screenshot at phone resolution; compute Feature Congestion clutter (Rosenholtz code) and ask raters which reads best and which "feels biggest". |
| Clumped vs even particle spacing | Only crowding theory found, no game study | A/B screenshots and a 1-second clip; time how long testers need to spot a marked hit spark among debris. |
| Vignette, chromatic aberration, radial blur values | No named source; Roblox has no built-in aberration or radial blur in the mirror | Prototype with ColorCorrectionEffect plus a UI overlay image; test at mobile size; limit by WCAG area and rate. |
| Exact flash duration (frames) | Only an uncredited tier C weak claim (1-2 frames) | Test 1, 2, 3, 4 frames at 60 and 30 fps; check WCAG flash rate. |
| Slow-motion depth and duration for finishers | Only "few frames" and ADSR shape | Test time scale 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 for 150-400 ms; note Roblox lacks a global time scale (inference), so slow the camera, animations and particles only. |
| Audio-visual sync tolerance for impacts | EBU R37 is for TV lip-sync | Test sound offset -40..+100 ms on a hit; mobile Bluetooth latency matters. |
| Nijman and Jonasson and Purho primary numbers | Videos not readable here | Watch the videos and take notes; verify the 10-20 ms hit freeze before relying on it. |
| Kao 2020 details (N, which effects per level) | ScienceDirect blocked (403) | Open the paper in a browser; or run our own 4-level test. |
| Does our Roblox physics debris freeze with hit-stop | Not in the docs mirror | Test in Studio: freeze animations and TimeScale vs Anchored/physics debris. |
| Phone comfort of shake and flash | GAG page for sudden movement has no shake numbers | Add a "reduce shake and flashes" setting; test with a few mobile players. |

## Verification log

Checked 2026-10-12 by an adversarial pass (claude-sonnet-5-5, low). Method: re-opened the cited URLs (PDFs were converted locally to text). No claim was proved false, so none were removed.

**Checked (24 claims or rows): 20 confirmed, 2 corrected, 2 unverified.**

| item | result |
| --- | --- |
| S01 hit-stop numbers, 70% figure, n=16, venue | confirmed (arXiv PDF and abs page: accepted at GEM 2022) |
| S02 trauma model, 3/22/73%, 2D vs 3D, quotes | confirmed against slide text |
| S23 Bevy constants | confirmed |
| S07 8-frame and 5-frame rule at 30 fps | confirmed |
| S19 WCAG numbers | confirmed |
| S20 EBU 40 ms / 60 ms | confirmed (TV only) |
| S13 Bouma 0.4-0.5, 150 ms | confirmed |
| S15 slope and attribute table | confirmed; generalisation of 20-50 ms corrected (single task) |
| S14 consensus, 150 ms, set size 4/6/10 | confirmed; "first stimuli to capture" unverified |
| S05 Kao 2024 | confirmed |
| S04 Johansen and Cook | confirmed; adversarial-game remark is the authors' speculation |
| S29 SmashWiki | Ultimate formula confirmed; Melee formula text garbled in fetch |
| S28 Nijman numbers | confirmed as quoted by the blog (still tier D, secondhand) |
| S08 Massoudi quote and FOV claim | confirmed |
| S11, S12 | unverified (abstract records not re-opened) |

**Cautions not fixed (judgement, left to the owner):**
- Tier A is applied to trade-press articles (S07 Song 2005, S08 Massoudi 2016) and a slide deck (S02). They are maker accounts, not peer review. Pre-2020 is marked, so the file is honest on age, but "A" overstates S07 and S08 for numbers such as the 8/5-frame rule (one game, one 30 fps clip).
- S01 is correlational (16 games, comment sentiment). The file says so; do not read "hit stop causes better feel" from it.
- The EBU limits are for TV lip-sync and are not a tolerance for game impacts. The file says so.
- The file only has fighting-game and Smash hit-stop numbers; the freeze values are fixed-60 fps and the ms conversions are the file's own arithmetic.

**Gaps and missing tier-A sources noticed:**
- Kao 2020 (Entertainment Computing) and Jonasson/Purho 2012 are the core "juice" papers and were read only secondhand.
- No peer-reviewed study of screen shake, flash or hit-stop timing on perceived impact was found; all numeric timing rests on practitioner sources.
- No source on motion sickness or comfort from shake/FOV change (e.g. VR FOV-reduction work) was read, yet the file proposes vignette and shake.
- Mobile-specific viewing (small screens, peripheral vision share) is not covered by any perception source; the crowding and eccentricity numbers assume larger fields of view.
